answer: Stop sybils with a timber quartz ferrous: an agent bonds one timber yard. Each cycle it drives one ferrous nail into a quartz-set beam; verifiers match its fracture to the yard chart, voiding a copied nail, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 yards at 18x: one nail is driven once into one beam, its quartz set by that timber's grain, unpullable for a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents hammer once, keep rights.
